{
  "proposition": "The proposed recurrence fits every supplied observation. Conditional on adopting it for every nonnegative integer n, x_n=5+3n+max(0,n-2), and x_5=23.",
  "evidence": "The exact observations are x_0=5, x_1=8, x_2=11, x_3=15, x_4=19. Their increments are 3, 3, 4, 4. No observation of x_5 or later values is supplied.",
  "prior_commitment_status": "The original universal +3 rule remains contradicted. Its earlier consistency with the first three observations and conditional prediction of 14 remain correctly qualified. The new recurrence accommodates the supplied counterexamples.",
  "calculation": "Summing the proposed increments gives x_n=5+3n+max(0,n-2): equivalently, 5+3n for 0<=n<=2 and 3+4n for n>=2. Thus x_5=23. The false twin 5+4n gives 5,9,13,17,21, contradicting observations at n=1,2,3,4.",
  "limitation": "The initial value and four increments are directly identifiable. Within the proposed single-threshold indicator family, they identify baseline 3, added increment 1, and threshold 2. Fit establishes compatibility only; the universal recurrence, physical mechanism, and future prediction lack empirical confirmation."
}
